note: Claims this repository has corrected, and must not state again. A correction that reaches one copy of a claim and leaves the others is the failure this list exists for; see scripts/check_retired_claims.py. Add an entry when you withdraw a claim that appeared in more than one place, naming the entry that withdrew it. Occurrences inside ledger/ are history and are never checked.

retired.phrase: a guard whose only witness is a suite you cannot run
retired.why: The suite runs here in --release; it is the debug build that does not fit. The guard has since been seen to fire as loader_cliff, exit 101.
retired.instead: Name the profile: the debug build is what exhausts the disk.

retired.phrase: the runner that does reach it cannot be built
retired.why: False as written. It cannot be built in debug on this container; --release is 131 MB and runs.

retired.phrase: docs/ is still out of scope, and deliberately
retired.why: check_cost_prose.py has walked docs/ since #283; the docstring paragraph was left behind by that widening.
retired.instead: site/ is out of scope; docs/ is read, with NOT_A_CLAIM for historical narration.

retired.phrase: nested loading were built afterwards in Rust and have
retired.why: N1 put a `path` of relationships on the wire, so nested loading crossed it. The claim was struck in docs/orm-comparison.md and left standing on site/docs/roadmap.html, which is the two-copies failure this list exists for.
retired.instead: A path resolves levels in one round trip; what it stops at is a predicate, ordering or limit per level.

retired.why: It does now, through the same parser the WHERE uses. The reason given for the limit — that the group-condition lists had no nested form to lower — was true of the spec and never of the kernel, whose Grouping::having has always been an Expr tree.
retired.instead: A HAVING brackets exactly as a WHERE does; a join's WHERE is the one clause that still takes AND only.

retired.phrase: because a check cannot hold one
retired.why: A check can hold a regular expression and always could; `~`, `~*`, `!~` and `!~*` have parsed since the last ClickBench query. That entry withdrew the claim in docs/validation.md's findings section and left it standing in the same file's 'What this note does not settle', which is the two-copies failure this list exists for -- here with both copies in one file.
retired.instead: A check can hold a regular expression; what is not built is evaluating one anywhere but the server.
